prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Launching Pet to Desktop", "Preparing desktop graphics engine and companion behaviors..."]
1: ["If your pet does not appear on your screen after loading, check your system tray or taskbar icon."]
2: ["Choose How Your Desktop Companion Comes to Life", "Select standard companion adoption or create a unique pet from photo upload."]
3: []
4: ["Compare Companion Characters", "Select your ideal companion character to start your adoption process."]
5: ["Sign In to Preserve Your Pet & Companion Progress", "Creating or signing into your account locks in your pets so they never reset or get lost."]
6: ["How to Control & Interact with Your Pet", "Right-click your companion on the desktop to open settings, start talking, or send your pet to the system tray."]
7: ["Preparing rendering assets and spawning desktop pet..."]
8: ["Your Companion is Ready to Explore Your Desktop!"]
9: ["Your Desktop Pet is Active!", "Your companion is now roaming your desktop screen. Click to say hello!"]
